#### What's great

dropping cmmnts onto a static site or blog is genuinely just one snippet - no separate backend to stand up or maintain. threads, markdown, mentions, and emoji cover what most doc pages and blogs actually need without pulling in a full community platform. the moderation basics (report threshold auto-hides a comment) mean you're not glued to a dashboard from day one either.

#### What needs improvement

same thing I asked in the comments - the system fingerprinting used to keep anonymous comments and mentions from becoming a moderation mess isn't mentioned anywhere I could find in the product itself. even a one-line note visible to the person commenting, not just the site owner's dashboard, would make the anonymous label feel more honest. [...] #### vs Alternatives

Discourse

looked at Discourse for a docs site, but that's a whole standalone forum you host and moderate as its own destination. we didn't want a separate community hub, just comments attached to the pages people already land on. cmmnts fit that scope better - lighter footprint, lives inside the existing site instead of next to it.
